description: Team BlindEye is dedicated to revealing what’s hidden in plain sight - transforming complex NASA Earth observations and soil datasets into actionable, climate-smart tools for sustainable agriculture.
summary:
We developed TerraShift, an explainable, farmer-centered easy-to-use decision-support platform that transforms NASA Earth observations into actionable, climate-resilient crop rotation strategies.

Addressing the dual crises of unpredictable weather and declining soil health, TerraShift harmonizes global satellite data including NASA POWER agroclimatology, SMAP root-zone moisture, ECOSTRESS evaporative stress, GPM precipitation, and SRTM topography -with local soil characteristics and farmer priorities. The platform pinpoints seasonal vulnerabilities like bare-soil erosion gaps and peak water deficits, benchmarking four rotation scenarios against the farmer's existing baseline. Each strategy provides transparent evidence cards detailing satellite observations, topsoil conserved, biological nitrogen gains, and local operational risks requiring agronomist review, supported by an interactive "What-If" climate stress simulator.

TerraShift is vital because it translates complex planetary data into transparent, farmer-friendly economic and agronomic metrics (fertilizer savings, topsoil protected) that empower local agricultural decision-making without replacing human judgment.
details:
TerraShift is a decision-support tool that helps farmers choose climate-resilient, soil-building crop rotations. A farmer picks a field on a map, enters coordinates, or starts from a demo location (Iowa, Kenya, Punjab or Spain). They select the one to three crops they currently grow and set four priority sliders: water conservation, soil health, erosion control and economic stability.

The system then pulls a 30-year climate baseline from NASA POWER and soil properties from ISRIC SoilGrids. An adapter layer adds SMAP, ECOSTRESS, GPM, GRACE and SRTM satellite data, and local fallback data keeps the tool working offline. From these inputs it calculates:

  • Water balance: reference evapotranspiration (Hargreaves-Samani), crop water demand and monthly deficits.
  • Erosion: annual soil loss using the RUSLE equation.
  • Nitrogen: a nitrogen budget that credits legumes for biological fixation.

It builds four rotations: the farmer’s current baseline, a soil-regeneration plan, a water-conservation plan, and a diversified cash-crop plan. A multi-criteria scorer ranks them using the farmer’s slider weights. Each plan includes an evidence card explaining why it was suggested, which NASA data supports it, the benefits, the information gaps and the risks needing local review.

Farmers can run a what-if stress test (rainfall from -50% to +50%, warming up to +5°C) to see which rotation holds up. A SMAP-based advisory recommends when to terminate the spring cover crop so it doesn’t drain moisture the next crop needs. Results can be exported as a print-ready agronomist brief.

Benefits and intended impact

Farmers get clear, jargon-light comparisons with concrete figures, such as topsoil saved per hectare and fertilizer savings (for example +$195/ha). Agronomists get an audit trail of satellite evidence and soil-water metrics, plus a ground-truth checklist before they endorse seed purchases.

The broader goal is to lower the perceived risk of regenerative farming. By making NASA Earth observations usable at field level and being honest about uncertainty, TerraShift aims to help more farmers move away from monocultures, conserve water and topsoil, and cut synthetic fertilizer costs. It supports decisions; farmers and agronomists keep the final call.

Tools and technologies

  • Backend: Python 3.11+, FastAPI with Uvicorn, Pydantic v2 and httpx for asynchronous requests.
  • Data: NASA POWER, ISRIC SoilGrids, SMAP, ECOSTRESS, GPM IMERG, GRACE/GRACE-FO, SRTM and Landsat/MODIS.
  • Frontend: a zero-build HTML5 app with Tailwind CSS, Leaflet.js and Lucide icons, plus an optional Vite/React version.
  • Engines: agronomy, multi-criteria scoring, rotation generation and stress testing.
  • Testing: an end-to-end suite covering API schemas, live-data fallback, all four strategies and a +2.5°C / -30% rainfall stress test.

No special hardware is needed, and a single startup script runs the whole app.

What makes it creative

  • Explainability first: every recommendation shows its reasoning, evidence, data gaps and risks instead of a single black-box answer.
  • Satellite data as inputs: NASA datasets drive actual calculations, such as SMAP setting a cover-crop termination window.
  • Farmer-driven ranking: the same field can yield different recommendations depending on the farmer’s priorities.
  • Stress testing: plans are tested against extreme weather rather than an average year.
  • Honest limits: the tool states what satellites can’t see, such as tile drainage and soil pan depth.

Factors considered

We designed for trust, so users can see why a plan is suggested. We accounted for local variability by flagging items that need on-the-ground testing. We kept economics central, since regenerative practices only work if the farm stays profitable. We reported satellite resolution limits openly, built fallbacks for areas with poor connectivity, and kept the interface simple for farmers while giving agronomists the detailed metrics. Finally, every result traces back to documented formulas and datasets, and automated tests protect the agronomy logic from regressions.
